Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Ajay Kumar Vashistha, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rajeev Dhar Dwivedi,
learned Aga for the State-respondent.

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
170 of 2023, under Sections 452, 376-D, 506 IPC, Police Station- Kasganj, District- Kasganj, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and co-accused Rinku and according to the FIR, on 05..03.2023 informant, who was a married lady, when alone in the house then co-accused Rinku dragged her in the dry drain and committed rape with her.
It is further mentioned in the FIR that applicant was guarding outside the drain.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that there is no allegation of rape against the applicant either in the FIR or in the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. but when her statement was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. then she started making allegation of Anand Pal vs State Of U.P. on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44616427/
1 rape also against the applicant along with co-accused Rinku.

sentences.text:
He further submitted that victim i.e.
informant of the case is major and married lady and entire story narrated by her appears to be improbable.
5. He further submitted that applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since 30.03.2023.

6. Per contra, learned AGA although, opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that neither in the FIR nor in the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. there was any allegation of rape against the applicant and victim is major and married lady.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. Although, victim in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. made allegation of rape also against the applicant along with co-accused Rinku but neither in the FIR nor in the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she made allegation of rape against the applicant.

9. Further, prosecutrix i.e. victim of the case is major and married lady and applicant is not having any criminal history and is in jail since 30.03.2023.
10.
Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
11. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant- Anand Pal be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
13.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

14. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the Anand Pal vs State Of U.P. on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44616427/
2 merits of the case during trial.
